subject.title: Consider file transfer for SSH-backed leases

question: Should `crabbox cp` become a cross-backend command whose core implementation handles every compatible `SSHLeaseBackend`, while delegated providers continue using opt-in native copy adapters?
rationale: Current architecture supports this direction, but maintainers must confirm the permanent command contract and decide which targets and path semantics are promised before implementation.

options.title: Add core SSH copy
options.body: Extend `cp` with provider-neutral upload and download over the resolved SSH transport, initially supporting POSIX SSH leases and adding other targets only with focused proof.

options.title: Support all SSH targets immediately
options.body: Define and implement one release covering POSIX, native Windows, WSL2, local-container, and proxy-backed SSH transports, accepting a larger compatibility and validation surface.

options.title: Keep cp provider-native
options.body: Retain the delegated-provider-only contract and require callers to use printed SSH commands or external transfer tools for SSH-backed leases.

recommendation.title: Add core SSH copy
recommendation.body: Extend `cp` with provider-neutral upload and download over the resolved SSH transport, initially supporting POSIX SSH leases and adding other targets only with focused proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice changes the top-level CLI contract and core/provider ownership boundary rather than requiring only a mechanical implementation decision.
